before: Can report activities, budgets and granted-project finances when KNCF requests
after: Standard or Collaboration: can report activities, budgets and grant finances when KNCF requests
why: Guideline §3 says items 1) and 2) do not apply to Basic A and Basic B; scoping is correct.

before: Has incorporated status or equivalent societal credibility as a voluntary organisation
after: Standard or Collaboration: incorporated, or a voluntary organisation with equivalent societal credibility
why: Same §3 exemption for Basic A/B; first-time and LDC grassroots applicants were wrongly ruled out before.

before: Has conducted nature conservation projects for at least 3 years
after: Standard or Collaboration: at least three years of nature conservation projects
why: 3-year track record is exempted for Basic A/B per §3; before wrongly excluded newer organisations from small grants.

before: Has appropriate cooperation from authorities, related organisations, NGOs and residents at project locations
after: Project has cooperation from government bodies, relevant international organisations, NGOs and residents at its sites
why: Matches the quote: government organizations and related international organizations, not generic related organisations.

before: No permanent-staff labour costs or full outsourcing; partial outsourcing is capped at 10% of the total grant amount
why: Before stated a grant cost exclusion as a project-wide prohibition; a budget rule rules no applicant out, so dropping it is right.

after: Basic B applicants are local grassroots organisations working in UN-designated Least Developed Countries
why: Verbatim §4 Basic B condition; a real track-specific hard rule, phrased so Yes qualifies.

after: Grant Review Committee screening
why: Accurate review stage with its quote, but every grant screens applications; adds little an applicant can act on.

before: For land purchases, land of at least 50 ha (25 ha for old broadleaf forest, lakes, mires, floodplains or coasts)
after: Land: ≥50 ha, or ≥25 ha for 100+ year broadleaf forest, long-continuity woods, lakes, mires, floodplains or coasts
why: FRL 2.1b: 100-year broadleaf and long habitat-continuity forest; 'old' was vague and the second forest class was missing.

before: For ambassador projects, an area with wilderness potential well over 50 ha
after: Ambassadors: ≥333 contiguous ha, or ≥166 ha if mostly floodplains, mires, lakes or coastal habitats
why: Hinweise §1 sets the concrete minimum (333/166 ha contiguous); before gave only the vague 'well over 50 ha'.

after: Extensions or infill can be smaller if the resulting site reaches the applicable 50 ha or 25 ha minimum
why: Either/or route split from the size rule and phrased as a permission; contradicts rule 1 in a yes/no checklist. Belongs folded into it.

after: Land: maximum 1,000 ha, with a 500 ha ceiling for floodplains, coastal areas and mires
why: Binding FRL 2.1 ceiling, stated separately from the minimums; a real hard rule.

after: Applicant has a registered office, establishment or branch in Germany
why: FRL §3 applicant seat rule, stricter than geography (which covers where work happens).

after: Nonprofits have statutory objectives relevant to the funding directive
why: FRL §3 condition on nonprofit applicants; hard rule, quoted verbatim from the call page.

after: Ambassador applicants are outside the top state level, including state ministries and statewide agencies
why: Accurate FRL §3 rule, but it only excludes ministries; irrelevant to operators and spends a scarce rule slot.

after: Ambassador area has a qualifying land project or a legally secured wilderness site suitable for expansion
why: Hinweise 7.3 states this as the prerequisite for ambassador funding; a decisive hard rule.
The Vorhabenbeschreibung is the proposal itself (Schritt 1); standards exclude the application from documents.

before: Private applicants new to ZUG: statutes and last two certified annual accounts
after: Private entities, no ZUG application in 6 months: statutes if applicable and last 2 certified accounts or substitute
why: Matches the Bonitätsprüfung: the test is a ZUG application within 6 months; statutes 'soweit zutreffend'; status report allowed instead.

before: Proof of third-party funds, if any
after: Evidence of third-party funds, if available or applied for
why: Quote covers funds available or applied for; small precision gain.

after: Land projects: qualified valuation report, or land-register extracts if the valuation is waived
why: Hinweise lists land-register extracts when no valuation is needed (pre-emption, bidding, de minimis); correct alternative.

after: Land projects: proof that the state was informed about the project
why: Required KWF attachment (FRL 7.1, Hinweise 2.2); applicants must obtain it before applying.

after: Work plan and timetable
why: Required for both KWF and KWB as a separate attachment in Hinweise 2.2.

after: Area shapefile in ETRS89/UTM
why: Required for both routes (land area or potential area); non-obvious technical deliverable.

before: Have no more than five years of paid conservation experience
after: Every team member is an early-career conservationist with at most five years of paid conservation experience
why: Quote applies the cap to all team members; before was ambiguous about whom.

before: Have all team members be nationals, unless one non-national is clearly justified
after: All members are host-country nationals, with one justified exception for a national of another eligible country
why: Adds the quote's condition that the exception be from an eligible country; legal kind fits nationality.

before: Have no team member employed or contracted by a CLP partner
after: No team member is a paid employee or contractor of a CLP partner from project development through implementation
why: Quote restricts paid employment/contracting; volunteers are only declared, so 'paid' avoids wrongly excluding them.

before: Go beyond academic research for any team member's degree
after: Project goes beyond members' degree research and has no direct link to a PhD or doctoral research
why: Same guideline bullet excludes projects tied to PhD research; verbatim extended quote supports it.

after: Contact CLP before applying if a team member has a listed nationality
why: Right, verbatim pre-application step, but appended after 'Full application, if invited'; steps must be in order.
